andhakavinda.notes: AN 5.114 and SN 6.13 both locate the Buddha at Andhakavinda in Magadha. AN 5.113 has the chapter heading, and AN 5.120 has the chapter recap. SN 6.12 and 6.14 are adjacent discourses.

andhavana.notes: The packet misses the grove because Sujato translates its name as Dark Forest. MN 23:1.3 has andhavane, and AN 10.7:4.2 has andhavanasmiṁ at Sāvatthī. Other explicit occurrences include SN 5.1–3, SN 5.10, SN 35.121 and SN 52.10. AN 6.49 names the residents Khema and Sumana, where the entry says Khema and Soma. AN 6.48, SN 35.120 and SN 52.9 are neighboring page hits.

anejakā.notes: DN 20:15.6 names the Anejakā beside the Accutā at the great assembly. The entry's DN ii 160 points to DN 16. Compare DN ii 260 for the Ariṭṭhakā in the same stanza.

annabhāra.notes: AN 4.30, AN 4.185 and MN 77 name the wanderer with Varadhara and Sakuludāyī. Thag 16.9:19–20 names a different Annabhāra, the poor fodder carrier whose life Anuruddha recalls. The packet has no entry for him. AN 4.28–29 and 4.184 do not name the wanderer.

anuruddha.notes: AN 1.192 names the foremost disciple in clairvoyance. Check the entry's account of the eight thoughts. In AN 8.30 Anuruddha reflects on seven in retreat and the Buddha supplies the eighth. His exchange with Sāriputta in AN 3.130 concerns his clairvoyance and lack of liberation. Several citations include adjoining texts, e.g. SN 9.5–7 includes the accounts of Ānanda and Nāgadatta on either side of Anuruddha in SN 9.6.

anurādha.notes: SN 22.86 and SN 44.2 both identify the monk in the wilderness hut near Vesālī. SN 44.1 concerns Khemā. SN 22.92 and SN 44.11 name Anurādha in chapter recaps. The entry also ends with a stray closing brace and comma.

anāthapiṇḍika.notes: AN 1.249 names the foremost donor as the householder Sudatta Anāthapiṇḍika. Many mentions give his monastery as the setting. The packet's AN 1.219–234 and 1.235–247 do not contain the donor identification. SN 55.25 concerns Sarakāni, while SN 55.26–28 name Anāthapiṇḍika.

araka.notes: AN 7.73 includes Araka in the list of teachers. In AN 7.74 he teaches the brevity of life. The entry draws the identification with the Bodhisatta from the Jātaka.

ariṭṭha.notes: MN 22 identifies the former vulture trapper. SN 54.6 gives the breathing exchange recounted in the monk's entry. SN 54.4–5 are adjacent texts. MN 116 explicitly calls Ariṭṭha a paccekasambuddha, and DN 32 lists him with Sūra, Rājā and Nemi in Vessavaṇa's realm. AN 6.120–139:1.19 explicitly calls a fourth Ariṭṭha an upāsaka. The packet has no entry for this layman.

ariṭṭhakā.notes: DN 20:15.3 names the Ariṭṭhakā alongside the Rojā. Sujato treats the flax-blue gods in the following line as a separate group, a reading the entry also records.

aruṇa.notes: DN 14:1.12.4 explicitly names King Aruṇa as Sikhī's father. SN 6.14 calls the king Aruṇavā, which DPD files under aruṇavant. DN 20:17.1 names the aruṇā deities, translated as the Dawn. DPD has a separate aruṇā sense for them on that word, but the packet omits both that sense and DN 20 from the allowed list.

aruṇavatī.notes: DN 14:1.12.6 calls Aruṇavatī King Aruṇa's capital. SN 6.14:2.2–3 gives King Aruṇavā's capital the same name and places Sikhī there. SN 6.15 mentions the name in the chapter recap.

asama.notes: SN 2.30:1.4 identifies the individual godling Asama by his verse on Pūraṇa Kassapa. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma. The entry itself treats a connection with the Asamā of DN 20 as conjectural.

asamā.notes: DN 20:14.2 has asamā ca duve yamā. DPD and DPPN read Asamā as a group alongside the Yama twins, as does Ṭhānissaro's translation. Sujato reads asamā as an adjective describing the twins, which explains the packet's zero mentions.

asibandhakaputta.notes: The first question in the entry, about rites for the dead, is in SN 42.6. The packet's citations begin at SN 42.7. All four encounters place the chief at Pāvārika's Mango Grove in Nāḷandā (pāvārikambavane). The entry calls the grove Pārileyyaka.

asita.notes: MN 116:6.14 lists the independent Buddha. The packet misses asito devalo isi in MN 93:18.6, where Sujato translates the name as Devala the Dark. Snp 3.11:1.4 also names Asita, the seer who visits the infant Bodhisatta. Neither seer has a candidate here.

asoka.notes: DN 14:1.11.1 names Vipassī's chief attendant. The candidate describes the deceased monk of Ñātikā in SN 55.9:1.2 and 2.1. SN 55.9:1.5 also names a layman Asoka. Only the deceased monk has a candidate. The entry's unplaced SN i 358 should read SN v 358.

asokā.notes: SN 55.9 explicitly distinguishes Asokā the bhikkhunī at 1.4 and Asokā the upāsikā at 1.6. The entry describes the nun. SN 55.10 lists other lay followers.

assaji.notes: The entry identifies Sāriputta's teacher and recounts Assaji's exchange with Saccaka in MN 35 and his illness in SN 22.88. MN 34 and SN 22.87 are adjoining discourses. MN 70:4.1 refers to the other Assaji through the separate compound assajipunabbasukā. That sense has no candidate.

assapura.notes: MN 39:1.2 and MN 40:1.2 both identify Assapura as an Aṅgan town. The entry names both discourses, but the citations place MN 38 and omit MN 40.

avanti.notes: The entry describes the kingdom. DN 19:36.5 names Māhissatī as the Avantis' capital. No candidate describes a city called Avanti. The packet misses the country lists in AN 3.70 and AN 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45, where the English name and Pali avantīnaṁ fall on different segments. MN 108:2.1 names King Pajjota in the episode cited by the entry.

avantiputta.notes: MN 84:2.1 names Avantiputta as king of Madhurā. MN 83 concerns King Maghadeva.

avīci.notes: Iti 89:5.3 explicitly names Avīci hell in the compound Avīcinirayaṁ, as the full entry observes. The bare avīci in DN 26:23.7 and AN 3.56:1.3 describes how closely people are packed together. MN 130 and AN 3.36 call the place they describe the Great Hell. The identification of that hell as Avīci comes from the commentary.

ayojjhā.notes: SN 22.95:1.1 places the Buddha at Ayujjhā on the Ganges. DPD gives ayujjhāyaṁ the town lemma ayujjhā, and Sujato writes Ayodhya. The packet misses this spelling. SN 35.241:1.1 reads Kosambī in the app's text, a variant the entry records. SN 22.94 and SN 35.240 are adjacent discourses.
